title: Achievements
items: 119 achievements across exploring, fighting, magic, crafting, music, pets, steeds, world events and a few secrets. Press Y (or find them in the Esc menu and the character panel).
Progress bars, points, chains to climb (I, II, III), search and filters; hidden ones stay ??? until you earn them.
Many come with gold, XP, items or a new title for your nameplate: pick it in the character panel.
Your old feats and titles carried over, and what you had already done counts.
Rumour has it a certain fire dash can do more than burn.

title: Loot that sparkles
items: Dropped items now glitter with little four-point glints in their rarity's colour, more and brighter the rarer they are.

title: More to do out there
items: Townsfolk have side quests (rescues, deliveries, hunts and more); helping a town earns renown.
Three story quests: The Lodestone's Hum, Embers of the Old Watch and The Bell Beneath.
World events pop up near you: a starfall, a caravan ambush and others. Watch for the red star on your compass.
Sealed vaults hide under ruins: solve the seal's puzzle, beat the keeper, open the chest.
Read 16 lore tablets, fill the bestiary, earn feats and wear titles (journal, J).
Gather herbs (E) and cook five new hearth recipes.

title: Spells, rebuilt
items: Every spell got new visual effects; high graphics goes all out.
14 new spells: hold-to-fire streams, homing souls, charged throws, orbiting blades, brands that chain, summoned allies.
Dashes are fast and last as long as you hold the key. Magma Dash flies like a jet; Glacier Step skates across water.
Other players now see your spells exactly as you do: same aim, same timing, same held poses.

title: Spirit steeds
items: Buy a Spirit Whistle at any general store (40 gold) and press 5: a spirit steed gallops in to you. E rides it, E (or Space standing still) gets off.
W trots, a Shift press spurs it to a gallop and a second spur bursts ahead (each spur costs stamina); S reins in and backs up; Space jumps fences.
It won't climb cliffs or wade into deep water, shies from demons at night, and a hard hit can throw you. Bows, staves, wands and spells work from the saddle.
Name it and pick its colour: Character (C), Your steed. Other players see you ride.

title: Taming and pet companions
items: Tame wolves, boars, slimes, rams, the Glintfox and more: carry a food it likes, weaken it, and when it stops to sniff the air, feed it (E). Stay close while the meter fills.
Your pet follows you, joins your fights, levels up and has an ability of its own: a healing slime, a howling wolf, a charging boar.
Press 6 to send it at what you aim at (hold 6 for the pet wheel), 7 to make it stay or follow, E beside it to pet it.
Pets are knocked out, never killed: they limp home to recover and come back. The rest wait in your stable at your camp or in any town (C, Your pets).
Some tamed creatures turn out shiny or elemental. The bestiary says which creatures can be tamed and what they like to eat.

title: Make camp
items: Press P to make camp: craft a kit, then place a campfire, a bedroll, a storage chest, a workbench or a signpost in the wild (wheel or R turns it, left mouse places it).
Gather firewood from fallen branches, or buy it at a general store.
A burning campfire keeps demons away at night, and you can cook on it.
Rest in your bedroll to wake Rested (faster healing, more stamina); it is also where you come back after a fall.
Your chest keeps 16 stacks, just for you or shared with your party; hold E on your own piece to pack it up again.

title: Weather that changes
items: Each region has its own weather now: clear skies, clouds, fog banks, drizzle, rain and thunderstorms; snow and blizzards on the peaks; heat haze and sandstorms in the badlands. Fronts roll in and out over a minute or two, and the clock shows a short forecast.
Thunderstorms throw lightning. It finds the tallest thing around, and anyone holding a sword or spear. If your blade crackles, switch to your bow or staff, fast.
Rain soaks the ground and greys the sky, and still makes climbing slippery. Lightning can set dry grass on fire.
Snow slows you down, and nights in the cold leave you Chilled (no health regeneration). Stay by a campfire, in town, or eat something warm like a stew.
Strong winds push your glider and your arrows. Fog hides you from enemies, and them from you.
Look for a rainbow after the rain.

title: Gone fishing
items: Buy a fishing rod from a general store or a tool merchant (or make one at a forge or your camp workbench), face a lake, river or the sea and press E.
Wait for the float to go under (a nibble is not a bite), strike, then reel: hold to pull in, let go when the line strains.
Fourteen kinds of fish live in different waters, biomes, hours and weather. A few are rare, and two are the stuff of legend.
Cook your catch at a hearth or campfire (thirteen new recipes), fill the new Fish tab in your journal (J) and earn four new feats.

title: A friendlier first hour
items: Press Esc for the new menu: every control in one place, sound, camera, tips and Leave.
Short tips show up when they matter instead of a wall of keys.
New characters start with "Slimes in the meadows": meet a townsperson, clear five slimes, collect your reward.
Quest markers now follow the person you are looking for, even when they leave work for the evening.
Getting downed tells you what got you, where you will wake up and that you keep everything.
After a respawn, enemies leave you alone for 5 seconds (or until you strike first).
This "What's new" panel, which shows what changed since you last played. The full list is in Esc, What's new.

title: Controls, tidied up
items: E does one thing at a time: whatever the [E] line under the crosshair says. In the saddle, E always gets you off.
The weapon technique moved from V to Tab, so talking on voice chat no longer swings it.
Esc, Controls lists every key, including fishing and photo mode.

title: Spell cards
items: The character screen (C) shows your spells as cards instead of dropdowns: each card shows its school, type (projectile, stream, homing, charge, summon...), tier, damage, mana and cooldown at a glance.
Hover a card (or tab to it) for everything else: range, status effects, how hard it hits with your gear, and which slots hold it.
Click a card and then a slot, or drag it onto a slot. The x clears a slot, and you can set up both loadouts from the same screen.
Text on the character screen is brighter and easier to read.

title: Graphics settings and art styles
items: New Graphics screen: the Graphics button at the top right, F10, or Esc > Graphics.
Pick a look: Lodestone (the new default), Painterly, Grim or Retro 32-bit.
Quality presets from Low to Ultra, chosen for your graphics card on first run, and you can change any single setting.

title: Play music
items: Carry a lute, a wooden flute, a hand drum or handbells (general stores and tool merchants, or make one at a camp workbench or a forge) and press U to play.

Your keyboard becomes the instrument: Q W E R… play a scale from its root, the number row an octave up, A S D… and Z X C… lower. Shift raises a note, Space accents it, the mouse wheel changes octave, the arrows change key and scale.
Players within 40 m hear you from where you stand, echoing in caves and halls. Press Enter for a metronome everyone near you shares.
Play for the townsfolk and they'll applaud. Play by a campfire at night and everyone by the fire rises Rested. Play 100 notes to become a Bard.

title: Monsters with character
items: Every creature has its own look now: squishy slimes with big eyes, boars with tusks, hooded bandits with real weapons, horned demons with glowing eyes, and bigger, grander bosses.
Enemies move like animals and fighters: they trot, hop, flap and look at you, wind up visibly before they strike, flinch when hit, reel when parried, and fall (or splat) when beaten.
Your summoned allies are glowing spirits in their element's colour.
Damage numbers are smaller, coloured by element, stack neatly, and crits pop.
Big crowds of enemies draw much faster.

title: Emotes
items: Hold H for the emote wheel: wave, bow, cheer, point, sit, dance, laugh, shrug, salute and rest by the fire.
Everyone nearby sees them. Tap H to repeat your last one, or type /emote wave in chat.

title: Photo mode
items: Press L for photo mode: the camera leaves your character and the HUD disappears.
Fly with WASD (Space and Ctrl for up and down), pick a visual style, preview any hour of the day, and add depth of field, vignette and film grain.
Press Enter to save a PNG. Esc frees the mouse, Esc again takes you back.

title: PvP and duels
items: Opt in to PvP from the character panel (C) or with /pvp. Towns and the Haven stay safe.
Challenge a party member to a duel from the party frame or with /duel. Duels stop at 1 health.

title: Third person and livelier players
items: Press T or the middle mouse button to switch between first and third person.
Other players walk, run, swing, cast, dodge and flinch instead of sliding around.

title: Skill tree and build overview
items: N opens the skill tree: every spell tree, what you can learn next and what it needs.
B opens your build: where your health, damage and armor come from, both loadouts side by side.

title: Around the world
items: Slime meadows around the Haven give new players something to fight close to home.
The map sketches the land you have walked, even before you climb a tower.
Fires stay small patches instead of eating whole hillsides.
Sound pass: rain sounds right under a roof, and loops and busy fights are calmer.
HUD tidy-up: level-ups, discovery cards and toasts no longer pile on top of each other.

title: Fixes from the first playtest
items: Voice chat works for everyone now, including local profiles.
Quest trackers and markers move on to the next step again.
You start with a pickaxe (older characters get one once).
Taking off a weapon gives you your training weapon back.
Travel to a friend from the Friends panel (O).
Reconnecting keeps your position instead of sending you back to spawn.
